sections.content: A good story links events by logic, not just by time. First choose the tense for when something happened, then the connector for how the events relate: sequence, contrast or consequence.

items.spanish: Busqué la cartera por toda la casa; sin embargo, no la encontré.
items.english: I looked for my wallet all over the house; however, I didn't find it.

items.spanish: Había perdido las llaves, así que llamé a mi hermana.
items.english: I had lost my keys, so I called my sister.

items.spanish: No tenía dinero para el autobús; por eso volví a pie.
items.english: I had no money for the bus; that's why I walked back.

items.spanish: Al final, un vecino me devolvió la cartera.
items.english: In the end, a neighbour gave me back my wallet.

sections.content: *Sin embargo* and *por eso* usually start a new clause, and *sin embargo* takes a comma after it. *Así que* joins two clauses inside one sentence. *Entonces* means "then" in a sequence, but "so" in conversation.
